items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I only met him a couple of times.

ctx.x: What was your – can you tell us about your personal intersection with him, when you met him, and or what your – how do you think he saw you? How did you see him? Because you were both people seriously writing about things in different spheres. He was a novelist and writing occasional essays. You’re a journalist at one point and then becoming an author. What was the dynamic between two people writing about loving the same thing, coming from different places?

I tell you, there wasn’t much of a dynamic. I only met him a couple of times. I don’t – he was on a level way above me as a novelist and as a figure. No, my interaction with him was reading about him. I didn’t know him that well. I remember, there was a party once though. I forget how it came out. People were talking about race and mixtures. Ellison drew himself up and said, “I have in me the blood of white Kentucky colonels.”
